questions.q: During the drill, what was the first clue that the latency problem wasn't inside checkout's own code?
options: Checkout's error rate spiked to 100%
Request rate stayed flat while p99 duration climbed
The checkout pods crashed and restarted
CPU usage on checkout pods dropped to zero
questions.explain: Rate staying flat while duration climbs points at saturation somewhere downstream rather than a problem in checkout's own request-handling code.

questions.q: What was the actual root cause of the flash-sale latency incident?
options: A bug in checkout's own payment-processing code
The inventory service's database connection pool was undersized and never load-tested for flash-sale volume
The AKS cluster ran out of nodes
The ACR registry was unreachable during the sale
questions.explain: The inventory service's DB connection pool saturated under flash-sale load, queuing every checkout request waiting on a stock check.

questions.q: Why did the alert that existed fire too late?
options: It was a full pool-exhaustion alert, not a saturation-based alert that fires earlier
Alertmanager was down during the incident
The alert was misconfigured to page the wrong channel
No alert of any kind existed on the inventory service
questions.explain: Only a full-exhaustion alert existed; it fired only after the pool was already fully exhausted, well after a saturation-based alert would have caught the trend.

questions.q: What is the core principle of a blameless postmortem?
options: Identify which engineer made the mistake and document it
Focus on what in the system allowed the incident, not who caused it
Skip root cause analysis and move straight to the fix
Only share the postmortem with management
questions.explain: A blameless postmortem asks what in the system allowed the incident to happen, focusing on systemic causes rather than individual blame.

questions.q: What makes a postmortem action item actually actionable, per this lesson?
options: It must be written in passive voice
It must reference the exact Prometheus query used in the drill
It must have a named owner and a due date
It must be approved by the whole engineering team before being logged
questions.explain: The guide states a postmortem without a named owner and date per action item is just a list of good intentions, not a fix.
